leads.summary: The locked-screen pointer-motion caller now sends unconditional DPMS enables, not only resume wakeups
leads.consequence: With the session still locked and the screen already on, each pointer-motion wake request can start another wake child after the preceding one exits. That child now dispatches DPMS enable even if all enabled monitors report on, unlike the old guard. Repeated requests are certain; whether they cause visible flashing on particular hardware requires hardware validation. This also applies to keyboard wake, failed password and unlock, not only suspend.

leads.summary: Open PR #12210 would send two global DPMS enables in succession on lid reopen
leads.location: bin/omarchy-system-wake:8; proposed bin/omarchy-system-lid-open:24-28 in omacom/omarchy PR #12210
leads.consequence: If #12210 is merged with this change unchanged, its lid-open path first runs omarchy-system-wake (now forced) and then explicitly sends the same global enable again. Previously the first enable could be skipped on a true status. Its comment explains the second call was to defeat precisely that guard, so it should be removed or consolidated if both PRs land. Real hardware flash is not established here.
leads.triage: factual; coordinator gh pr view/diff (coord/pr-12210.diff lines 57-62, PR open); Opus draft check confirmed read-only

leads.summary: Open PR #9108's per-monitor DPMS branch conflicts with global forced wake and the new assertion
leads.location: bin/omarchy-brightness-display:37,70-80; proposed bin/omarchy-brightness-display on branch in omacom/omarchy PR #9108
leads.consequence: If the two changes are combined without distinguishing a bare wake from an explicit --monitor request, the focused-monitor helper normally supplies a nonempty monitor, so #9108 sends a command containing monitor = eDP-1 instead of the global enable expected by this PR. No global dispatch is sent to other enabled monitors. The new brightness test's hyprctl stub logs that targeted command instead of the asserted global command, making its --force assertion fail on a straight combined branch. This is a conditional merge conflict, not a defect of the pinned head alone.

leads.summary: New --force option is not offered by shell completion for omarchy brightness display
leads.consequence: At `omarchy brightness display <TAB>`, discovery of `omarchy-brightness-display-apple` and `omarchy-brightness-display-ddc` already produces nonempty candidates, so the completion function never reaches the metadata branch and never offers `--force` (nor the previously existing options). Even without those child binaries, the positional metadata selects only `[--no-osd]` at the first argument, not the new `[--force]`. The flag still works when typed by hand.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** The `--force` flag works as written: `--force on` always sends the DPMS enable and plain `on` keeps the skip.

**Outcome:** Hyprland's source drops a DPMS enable for any monitor it already marks on, so the forced dispatch is unlikely to re-light the panel in the state described in #13251. The new `--force on` test also fails at this head.

### Hyprland ignores the forced enable when `dpmsStatus` is already true

Per Hyprland v0.56.2 source (not tested on hardware):

- `hl.dsp.dpms({ action = "enable" })` reaches [`Actions::dpms`](https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/blob/v0.56.2/src/config/shared/actions/ConfigActions.cpp#L1236-L1260), which calls `setDPMS(true)` on each enabled monitor.
- [`CMonitor::setDPMS`](https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/blob/v0.56.2/src/output/Monitor.cpp#L2310-L2314) returns early when `m_dpmsStatus == on`, so nothing is committed to the output.
- `dpmsStatus` in `hyprctl monitors -j` is [that same `m_dpmsStatus` field](https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/blob/v0.56.2/src/debug/HyprCtl.cpp#L283). It records Hyprland's last DPMS request, not the panel's actual state.
- The same early return is present in v0.55.0 through v0.56.2 and on current `main`, which covers every release that accepts the `hl.dsp.dpms` syntax.

```text
Hyprland state (per monitor)              base `on`               head `--force on`
some enabled monitor dpmsStatus=false     dispatch -> commit      dispatch -> commit
all enabled monitors dpmsStatus=true      no dispatch             dispatch -> early return, no commit
```

**Impact:** In the reported state (`dpmsStatus=true` while the panel is dark), head and base leave the output untouched, so #13251 likely stays unfixed. For the same reason, the extra dispatch is not expected to cause the unlock-screen flash that the guard was added to prevent.

**Suggested change:** Establish on the affected laptop what actually re-lights the panel before choosing where to hook recovery:
- capture `hyprctl monitors -j` while the panel is dark;
- check the Hyprland log for `Couldn't commit output ... for DPMS = true` and `Couldn't retry committing output ...`;
- compare a lone `enable` dispatch with a `disable` followed by `enable`.

If an off/on cycle is what works, limit it to the affected case (a disable/enable cycle visibly blanks the panel on healthy hardware too) and run it from a real resume event (for example `PrepareForSleep(false)`, where the workaround in #13251 ran) rather than from `omarchy-system-wake`. `omarchy-system-sleep-monitor` currently handles only the pre-sleep signal.

**Related:** Open PR #12210 adds a direct global `hl.dsp.dpms({ action = "enable" })` after `omarchy-system-wake` in its lid-open path, to get around the same guard. Per the source above, that dispatch would also be dropped while `dpmsStatus` is true.

### The new `--force on` test fails at this head

The mock logs `printf 'hyprctl %s\n' "$*"`, which records `hyprctl dispatch hl.dsp.dpms({ action = "enable" })` without single quotes. Both new greps search for `dispatch 'hl.dsp.dpms(...)'` with single quotes, so they never match. Stock run at head (isolated sandbox, stubbed `hyprctl`):

```text
ok - on skips DPMS enable when every panel already reports lit
not ok - --force on dispatches DPMS enable despite stale dpmsStatus
```

The file exits 1. The `on skips` check cannot fail: it still passes with the guard deleted.

**Impact:** Test-only. The changed test file fails at head, and its `on skips` check does not detect removal of the guard.

**Suggested change:** Drop the single quotes from both patterns:

```diff
-if grep -F "dispatch 'hl.dsp.dpms({ action = \"enable\" })'" "$call_log" >/dev/null; then
+if grep -F "dispatch hl.dsp.dpms({ action = \"enable\" })" "$call_log" >/dev/null; then
...
-grep -F "dispatch 'hl.dsp.dpms({ action = \"enable\" })'" "$call_log" >/dev/null || \
+grep -F "dispatch hl.dsp.dpms({ action = \"enable\" })" "$call_log" >/dev/null || \
```

With that change, the test passes at head, fails on base at the `--force` case, and fails for both a deleted guard and a `--force` flag that is parsed but ignored. It remains a script-level check against a mocked `hyprctl` and cannot show that the panel re-lights.

### `omarchy-system-wake` runs on lock-screen input, not only after resume

`omarchy-system-wake` is not called on resume. It runs from:
- the lock screen on key presses, text changes, mouse movement and clicks (`shell/plugins/lock/LockView.qml` emits `wakeRequested`, and `shell/plugins/lock/Service.qml` starts one `omarchy-system-wake` run per wake request unless a run is still in progress);
- password submit, failed authentication and unlock;
- a cancelled idle cycle (`shell/plugins/services/idle/Service.qml`).

Commit 54d79d9d added the guard for exactly this lock-screen keystroke path. With `--force` in `omarchy-system-wake`, no in-repo caller still uses the guard. The PR's commit message ("Keep that guard for keystroke wake"), the PR description ("the keystroke path still trusts the status") and the new code comment ("for the wake path only") therefore do not match the call sites.

**Impact:** Given the Hyprland early return above, no visible change is expected on healthy hardware, but each lock-screen input burst now sends a dispatch instead of a status query.

**Suggested change:** Correct the description and comment, or, if the intent is resume-only recovery, hook a resume event as suggested above.

**Verified** in the sandbox at head and base:
- `--force` is accepted in any order with `--no-osd` and `--monitor` before the step.
- `--force +5%`, `--force --monitor DP-1 50%` and bare `--force` behave identically to the same commands without the flag, and `--force off` sends only the disable dispatch.
- Plain `on` still sends the enable when any enabled monitor reports off, the monitor list is empty, or the query fails.
- `omarchy-system-wake` keeps its call order.
- The new `monitor-recovery-test.sh` grep passes at head and fails on base.
- The `omarchy:args` metadata keeps all arguments optional (checked from source).
